newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Yugoslavia says opposition wins Belgrade.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia says opposition wins Belgrade.

text.p: Yugoslavia on Friday acknowledged that opposition parties won a majority in nine municipalities in Belgrade in November 17 local elections but said it still needed more detail to clarify results in others towns.

In a letter from Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic to the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), Belgrade said the "coalition 'Zajedno' won the majority in nine municipalities in Belgrade".

The letter was sent as a response to an OSCE report by former Spanish prime minister Felipe Gonzalez who led a mission to Serbia to investigate the disputed elections. The OSCE sent Gonzalez after an invitation from Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic who has faced 46 days of protests over cancellation of the opposition victories in municipalities across the country.
Milutinovic's letter said the results in Serbia's second biggest city, Nis, were still being studied.

He said the opposition won the election in Uzice, Kragujevac and Zrenjanin but no party had won a majority in Pirot, Pancevo and Jagodina. Gonzalez's report had said the opposition had won the election in all these municipalities.
Milutinovic also called for more data relating to six other municipalites where Gonzalez said the opposition had won.
